name: Kasbah of the Udayas
hero_subtitle: White-and-blue quarter above the Bouregreg mouth — gates, terraces and Atlantic views.

overview.title: The postcard corner of the capital
overview.p1: The Kasbah of the Udayas crowns the cliff where the Bouregreg meets the ocean. Inside the Almohad gate, lanes painted in white and blue lead to terraces, the platform overlooking Salé, and the Andalusian Gardens. It is Rabat’s most photogenic historic quarter — and still a lived-in neighbourhood.
overview.p2: Come early for quieter streets and clearer light on the river. Pair the kasbah with the medina below or a tea at Café Maure before continuing to Hassan Tower.

food.title: Eating near the Udayas
food.p1: Café Maure is the classic tea stop inside the kasbah. Fuller meals sit in the medina a short walk downhill.
food.p2: Use the kasbah for atmosphere; book medina houses for dinner.
food.li5: Evening tables: Dinarjat or Dar Naji.

faq.title: FAQ about Kasbah of the Udayas

q1.question: Is entry free?
q1.answer: Walking the kasbah streets is free; small museums or towers may charge.

q2.question: How long do I need?
q2.answer: Ninety minutes to two and a half hours with gardens and viewpoints.

q3.question: Café Maure still open?
q3.answer: Usually yes for tea and pastries — hours can vary.

q4.question: Combine with the medina?
q4.answer: Yes — downhill into the medina lanes toward Rue des Consuls.

q5.question: Best photo spot?
q5.answer: The platform overlooking the Bouregreg and Salé.
